name: Male infertility due to obstructive azoospermia
aliases: Male infertility secondary to ductal obstruction

criteria.description: Confirmed absence of spermatozoa in ejaculate on at least two semen analyses
Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels within normal range indicating preserved spermatogenesis
Evidence of obstruction in the male reproductive tract via imaging or surgical exploration
Normal testicular size and consistency on physical examination
Exclusion of genetic causes such as Y-chromosome microdeletions or congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of azoospermia confirmed by semen analysis, normal serum FSH levels, and evidence of ductal obstruction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of non-obstructive causes of azoospermia and genetic testing to rule out congenital causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal secondary sexual characteristics with infertility
searchTerms: healthy secondary sexual traits with infertility
normal puberty signs with fertility problems

common.notes: Often associated with ejaculatory duct obstruction

common.symptomName: Normal serum FSH and LH levels

occasional.notes: May occur if obstruction causes epididymal distension

searchTerms: history of infections in reproductive tract

occasional.notes: Thickening or absence may be noted
searchTerms: abnormal vas deferens felt on exam
vas deferens abnormalities detected by touch

occasional.notes: Occasionally present due to chronic obstruction

rare.symptomName: Associated congenital anomalies of the urinary tract
searchTerms: urinary tract malformations present at birth

laboratory: Azoospermia confirmed on at least two semen analyses
Normal serum FSH and LH levels
imaging: Transrectal ultrasound showing dilated seminal vesicles or ejaculatory duct obstruction
Scrotal ultrasound demonstrating normal testicular morphology and possible epididymal dilation
genetic: CFTR gene mutation testing to rule out congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens
other: Physical examination revealing normal testicular volume and palpable vas deferens
Surgical exploration or vasography confirming site of obstruction

distinguishingFeatures: Absent vas deferens on physical exam
Often normal or low ejaculate volume

redFlags: Sudden onset of scrotal pain with swelling
Presence of testicular mass or asymmetry
Elevated serum FSH indicating primary testicular failure
references: Jarow JP, et al. Evaluation of the azoospermic male. J Urol. 2010;183(4):1334-1341.
